verses.1: After that, it was the feast day of the Jews. Then Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.2: In the Holy City, there is a swimming pool that is called Ebreisti Bethesda. It has five lanes.
verses.3: In those places, there was a large number of the sick, blind, deaf, and those who suffered from various diseases.
verses.5: There was also a man who was thirty-eight years old at that time, and he was very sick.
verses.6: When Jesus saw that he was lying down, and realizing that it had been a long time since he had eaten, he said to him, “Do you want to get well?”
verses.7: The sick man replied, “Lord, I don’t have anyone to whom I can entrust myself when there’s trouble with the water. I’ll go to another place where someone else will take care of me.”
verses.8: Jesus said to him, “Get away from that tree and walk away.”
verses.9: And immediately, the man became healthy again. He also cured his leprosy. It happened on a Saturday.
verses.10: So, the Jews said to the cured man, “It’s Saturday today; you shouldn’t go out in such a state.”
verses.11: And he said to them: “The one who healed me said to me, ‘You must take care of your snake and watch over it carefully.’”
verses.12: They therefore asked him, “Who is this man who says these things to you? What kind of person is he?”
verses.13: But the blind man didn’t know who Jesus was. After all, Jesus had sent away the crowd from that place.
verses.14: After this, Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Look, you are healed. No longer suffer from any more pain, so that nothing bad may happen to you.”
verses.15: The man went away and told the Jews that Jesus was the one who had healed him.
verses.16: And because of this, the Jews reproached Jesus for doing these things on Sabbath day.
verses.17: He replied to them, “My father works until breakfast time, and I also work.”
verses.18: Therefore, the Jews wanted to kill him even more because he not only abolished the Sabbath, but also called God his own father, treating Him as if He were equal to himself.
verses.19: So Jesus said to them, “Truly, I say to you, no son can do anything without seeing his father doing what he does. For whatever the father does, the son will also do.”
verses.20: For the father loves his son, and all things show him what he has done. He also shows him more of his works, so that you may be amazed.
verses.21: For just as the father raises the dead and brings them back to life, so too does the son who wants to bring people back to life.
verses.22: For the father also does not judge anything; instead, he gives all judgment to his son.
verses.23: So that everyone will honor the son as they honor their father. Those who do not honor the son, in fact, are not honoring the father who sent him.
verses.24: I say to you truly, that whoever hears my words and believes them will have eternal life. He will not go to judgment, but will be transferred from death to life.
verses.25: I say to you, now is the time when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear it will live.
verses.26: For just as the father has life within himself, so too he gave his son life to have it within himself.
verses.27: And he was given the authority to make judgments, because he was indeed a human child.
verses.28: Do not marvel at this, that a time comes when all those who are in the tombs will hear his voice.
verses.29: And those who have done good deeds will be sent to life after death. And those who have done evil deeds will be sent to judgment after death.
verses.30: I cannot do anything by myself. As I hear and judge, my judgment is indeed just: I do not pursue my own desires, but those of the one who sent me.
verses.31: If I testify about myself, then my testimony is not true.
verses.32: The other witnesses about me are also different. I know that the testimony they give about me is true.
verses.33: You sent for John, and he testified truthfully.
verses.34: I, however, do not receive testimony from people. I say these things so that you may be saved.
verses.35: That was the tomb that was supposed to be there, and it indeed appeared. But you, however, wanted to be grateful to heaven in its light.
verses.36: But I have a greater testimony than John. For the works that my Father has given me to complete, those very works testify about me that my Father sent me.
verses.37: And that man who sent me there also testified against me. You never heard his voice, nor did you ever see his face.
verses.38: And you don’t have his words in your possession. You don’t believe what that person said to you.
verses.39: Look at those writings; it seems to you that you can have eternal life through them. And those who testify about me are also witnesses in this regard.
verses.40: And you don’t want to come to me so that you can live.
verses.41: I do not receive glory from people.
verses.42: But I knew that you do not possess the love of God within yourselves.
verses.43: I have abandoned the name of my father; do not accept me then. If someone else comes with his own name, then you may accept him instead.
verses.44: How can you believe, when you receive glory from each other? And why do you not seek that glory that comes only from God alone?
verses.45: Do not think that I am accusing you of anything against your father. It is Moses who is the one who accuses you. You have trusted in him.
verses.46: For if you believe in Moses, then you must also believe in me. For he wrote about me there.
verses.47: And if you don’t believe those letters, then how can you believe our letters?
